class.name: TerrainRenderer
class.brief_description: Draws the active city's terrain: its 4 m tiles and ring as LOD chunks, and a coarse horizon beyond them.
class.description: Reads the [code]terrain.tiles[/code] snapshot data and the active city from [CitySim] every frame. Each 2,048 m tile is a quadtree of chunks chosen by their geometric error on screen; meshes are built on worker threads and only chunks of tiles that changed are built again. Beyond the active tiles it draws the map's 32 m DEM and then its region raster out to [member horizon_radius]. Positions are in the active city's local frame (meters from its south-west corner, x east and z north) and are drawn with Godot z = -north, so the map is not mirrored ([code]Sim.to_view()[/code] converts). Keep the node at the origin.

method.name: get_city_id
method.description: Returns the id of the city whose terrain is shown, or 0.

method.name: get_city_origin_tile
method.description: Returns the south-west tile of the active city's area, the origin of its local frame.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: Returns the ground height at a city-local point ([param x] east, [param z] north of the city's south-west corner; Godot's z is the negative of it): the active tiles where they are, else the map's 32 m DEM or region raster. NaN without a map.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns [code]{tiles, chunks_drawn, chunk_meshes, triangles_drawn, horizon_triangles, jobs_pending, mesh_bytes, ready}[/code]. [code]ready[/code] is true once every chunk the view wants is built.

method.name: has_terrain
method.description: Returns true while an active city's terrain is shown.

method.name: pick_terrain
method.description: Returns the ground point under a screen position as a [Vector3] in the city-local frame (east, height, north), the frame commands use, or [code]null[/code] where the ray misses the active tiles. Its position in the scene is [code]Sim.to_view()[/code] of it.

members.member: Whether the active tiles cast shadows. The horizon never does.
How many tiles around the active tiles are drawn from the 32 m DEM (at 64 m) before the region raster takes over.
How far from the city's center the horizon reaches, in meters.
How many chunk meshes are kept; the ones unseen for longest are freed beyond this.
A chunk is split while its geometric error covers more than this many pixels.
The finest LOD for ring tiles (outside the city's area): 1 means 8 m.
A chunk is also split while the camera is closer than this many times its size.
Main-thread milliseconds per frame spent handing finished chunk meshes to the renderer.

signal.name: terrain_changed
signal.description: Emitted when another city's terrain starts to be shown (or none: id 0).
